gen-gf-comic-neue-fs-asap: Asap reads crisp and sturdy, its lowercase standing nearly as tall as the capitals. And Comic Neue's rope-thin handwriting gives it a friendly counterpart with the same openness in every curve.
gen-gf-comic-neue-fs-bespoke-serif: Loose, hand-drawn charm up front. Comic Neue keeps every stroke rope-thin and friendly, while Bespoke Serif brings a text serif's dignified, high-contrast authority that holds up best when you take it in gently.
gen-gf-comic-neue-fs-epilogue: Friendly through and through. Comic Neue does its best work with casual, pen-drawn warmth in a moderate lowercase, whereas Epilogue's tall, curvy, wire-like sans body is what carries the text.
gen-gf-comic-neue-fs-erode: Comic Neue's rope-thin, pen-and-paper lettering is the first thing you notice, with no thick or thin parts anywhere. Erode answers with a tall middle band and a gentle ebb and flow of weight, which would make a shrunken heading look slight beside it.
gen-gf-comic-neue-fs-fira-sans: Fira Sans brings a large x-height and s curves that open wide at both ends, with no thick and thin contrast at all. But Comic Neue's casual handwriting supplies the warmth, so the pair feels approachable without losing its sturdiness.
gen-gf-comic-neue-fs-public-sans: Public Sans has a hefty lowercase and broad open counters, so it feels sturdy from the first line. Public Sans keeps that trustworthy weight over a longer stretch, while Comic Neue's marker-nib heading stays loose above it.
gen-gf-comic-neue-fs-supreme: Crisp from the first line, Supreme forms a thick, heavy-looking strip of text with letters held open. And a longer passage in it moves along cleanly, with Comic Neue's casual handwriting making the headings feel friendly.
gen-gf-comic-neue-general-sans: General Sans fills the line with a tall x-height and smooth curves, pressed down with steady confidence. Pairing it with Comic Neue's lower, handwritten headings works nicely if you give the headings a bit more size.
gen-gf-comic-neue-gf-bhutuka-expanded-on: BhuTuka Expanded One reads slowly, almost at a leisurely walk, with curvy letters and thin joins as sturdy as its stems. And Comic Neue's handwritten, rope-thin headings lighten that literary seriousness without ever fighting it.
gen-gf-comic-neue-gf-kiwi-maru: Kiwi Maru reads in a traditional, editorial way, with terminals stopping far from the stem and generous letterspace throughout. Make Comic Neue's heading too small and it gets lost.
